rationale: B wins because it keeps the facts on a leash. Its line "whether it also uses the new on-device model, since the facts do not say so" catches the trap A walks straight into with "The Factory That Runs AI Without a Cloud Connection." A has more furniture, but some of it is cardboard: the factory/offline story is one customer call away from collapsing.
gaps_in_A: "The Factory That Runs AI Without a Cloud Connection" invents the customer use case. The update says a Fortune 100 manufacturer is an early enterprise customer, not that a factory is running offline AI.
"a Fortune 100 manufacturer already using it" wrongly fuses the on-device model with the enterprise customer. That connection is not in the supplied facts.
"Good Enough for a Fortune 100 Factory" states capability and deployment as fact while the benchmark is unreproduced and the customer workload is unknown.
"five distinct shapes exist" is inflated. The category, customer, and licensing angles all lean on the same unsupported offline-enterprise bridge.
gaps_in_B: "is paying Hugging Face to keep its models private" overstates motive and commercial status. Early enterprise customer plus private hosting makes it plausible, not proven.

"The prevailing belief is that reasoning quality tracks parameter count" imports a broad market premise that is not in the update. It works as framing, but it needs outside support before becoming pitch language.
It misses a cleaner enterprise IT/procurement angle. The set has developer edge and manufacturing trade, but leaves the SSO/audit/private-hosting buyer story mostly inside the customer angle.
